column1: # Native unit personality adaptation sources, extracted from PE:6a70a6d9:02711000.
# Read-only disassembly: fixed w64devkit-2.9.1/bin/objdump.exe, Intel x86-64 syntax.
# unit.current_soul = pointer at unit+0xa98; soul.personality begins at soul+0x248.
# unit.misc_traits vector begin/end = unit+0x9a8/unit+0x9b0; each pointer targets int16 id at +0 and int32 value at +4.
# misc_trait id 13 = WantsDrink, original ALCOHOLIC; first matching entry is used. No matching entry omits the alcohol sentence.
# likes_outdoors = signed int32 soul+0x374 (personality+0x12c); combat_hardened = signed int32 soul+0x378 (personality+0x130).
# This paragraph uses unit.sex byte at unit+0x12e; preceding personality helpers instead use soul.sex byte at soul+0x84.
# subject formatter 0x140aa4730: sex 1 -> he, sex 0 -> she, all other values -> it; r8b != 0 uppercases the initial byte.
# <He/She/It> and <he/she/it> are dynamic subject families, not literal native strings. Each represents three grammatical outputs.
# Alcohol comparisons and hardening ranges are signed. Outdoor equality and hardening==100 are exact; hardening>100 selects hardened individual.
# Paragraph order: alcohol, outdoors, combat hardening. Native color prefix is [C:7:0:1], with period and two spaces after each sentence.
# With a soul but no visible adaptation sentence, native control flow can retain only the color prefix; this is not a missing prose branch.
# This is a decompiled source inventory; it does not claim an observed game display result.
